Rishi,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're ramping the Catalyst <> Redwood integration and just noticed account/territory overlap that could blow up into partner conflict if we don't lock ownership now. Internal snapshot attached (catalyst_account_map.csv) — shows multiple coverage flags for the same named accounts in North America where both Lumen Partners and an ISV implementer (Mercurio) are actively engaged.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood hold a 30-day escrow on co-sell/lead submission for the named accounts while we arbitrate ownership?
- Can we get a mutual action plan (MAP) that splits technical integration ownership from commercial ownership so all parties are clear?

We prefer Redwood to own the escrow gating (simple form, not legal heavy) and for integration responsibilities to be assigned to the implementer. We want to avoid double-commitment on demos and avoid partner conflict during procurement.

Attaching account map. Happy to jump on a short call — Evan

Attachments: catalyst_account_map.csv

Evan — thanks for the clear summary and the map. We can absolutely do a temporary escrow for lead submissions while the parties confirm ownership. Proposal in this message:

1) Redwood will hold a 30-day escrow window for the accounts listed in your CSV. During that period, no co-sell credits or pipeline submissions will be accepted from competing partners for those accounts without a joint confirmation email.
2) Split of responsibilities:
   - Technical integration and implementation scope: implementer (Mercurio / consultant) owns delivery and first-response technical support.
   - Commercial lead handling / deal owning: primary partner designation (Lumen or Catalyst) will be recorded in the MAP and HubSpot deal.
3) MAP: we'll circulate a short Mutual Action Plan (one-pager + owner table). I've attached a first draft (MAP_proposal_v1.xlsx) — Marissa can take the lead on the owner table and technical column.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to confirm technical owner assignments and estimated timelines (by EOD Wed).
- Laura to validate co-sell accounting rules and whether we need a temporary flag in HubSpot (by Thu).
- Evan, if you can confirm procurement contact (who will sign any brief SOW / procurement paperwork), we can loop them in.

Happy to run a 20-minute sync if that helps.

Best,
Rishi
VP, Alliances | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Operational asks for us:
- Marissa: take ownership of the MAP owner table. For each account in the CSV, assign: implementer (tech owner), primary commercial partner, and fallback. Please add SLA for technical handover (e.g., demo, runbook delivery).

Proposed timeline: 30-day escrow active starting when Evan confirms procurement contact and we publish MAP. If we can't get two-party confirmation within 30 days, we escalate to arbitration (channel ops + legal).

I'm attaching the MAP draft. Also note: we should consider a simple escrow acceptance email template so we can close this quickly.

Thanks — R
